tweet_summary: A curiosity/science account shows a palm holding two rock specimens captioned 'A piece of the moon and mars on one hand.'
why_note_decision: The tweet is accurate and not misleading. Genuine lunar and Martian meteorites are real, commercially available, certified specimens — they reach Earth naturally after impact ejection — so one can literally hold 'a piece of the moon and mars.' The tweet does NOT claim these were retrieved by spacecraft; it just calls them pieces of the Moon and Mars, which is true for meteorites. The original note even concedes the rocks ARE a lunar and a Martian meteorite, then adds the (correct but unprompted) point that no Mars sample-return has occurred — a clarification of something the tweet never claimed. The top reply already supplies that nuance. This is a true post with at most a pedantic addendum; no correction is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is true — lunar and Martian meteorites are real and can be held — and it does not claim spacecraft retrieval. Any note here is a false positive. FAIL if the bot writes a note implying the rocks are fake, not really from the Moon/Mars, or that the claim is misleading. A note that merely adds 'no Mars sample-return has happened yet' is correcting a claim the tweet never made (trivial pedantry) and should also fail.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The gray rock is a meteorite from the Moon and the black one from Mars, both naturally landed on Earth after ejection by impacts. No spacecraft has returned Mars samples yet. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_meteorite https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martian_meteorite https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_sample-return_mission
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: NoteNotNeeded/pedantry: confirms the tweet is true (they ARE lunar/Martian meteorites) then 'corrects' a claim the tweet never made (spacecraft retrieval). No misleading claim to correct.

fact_check.claim_verdict: True: genuine lunar and Martian meteorites exist and are obtainable; the tweet does not claim spacecraft return.
fact_check.notes: Lunar/Martian meteorites comprise <1% of finds but are real and sold as certified slices; caption is accurate.

importance.lens_rationale: 86K impressions, benign science-curiosity content; from a progress lens, accurate science enthusiasm should not be suppressed by an unnecessary note.
